[h1]21/04/23 Playtest Build - Patch Notes[/h1]

[h2]Combat[/h2]

[h3]Weapons[/h3]
[list]
[*] There is a brand new battle rifle model (with new animations and new audio).
[*] There is a brand new plasma rifle model (with new animations and new audio).
[*] All plasma rifles that consume more than 1 energy per shot have had their damage output reduced.
[*] The damage clouds spawned from the Toxic plasma rifle modules have had their durations reduced to 3 seconds (down from 5).
[*] The ‘Shield Burster’ plasma rifle ammo module has had its AoE damage increased.
[*] All cluster strike ammo modules (for sniper rifles) have had their bullet damage reduced.
[*] The hip fire bullet spread from sniper rifles has been nerfed. The base spread has been doubled. The amount of spread addition when landing from a jump has been increased, the delay before it fades off has been increased, and the rate at which it goes away has been reduced.
[*] The time to aim down sights with sniper rifles has been increased by 20%. The hyper rifle has had its ‘aim down sights’ time reduced further.
[*] The ‘Light - Tri-Shot’ and ‘Heavy - Tri-Shot’ sniper ammo modules have had their damage reduced, fire rate reduced, spread increased, but the fall-off and effective range penalties removed.
[*] Battle rifles and plasma rifles have had the ‘landing spread fade delay’ (the time it takes for the additional spread that comes when landing from a jump) increased. The rate at which it then fades has been slowed down.
[*] Semi-automatic battle rifles have had their vertical recoil variance drastically reduced to make them more reliable at long ranges. On the flip-side, the bullet spread from hip fire now goes up at a faster rate from consecutive shots, making them a bit less effective in close quarters.
[*] Melee range has been slightly increased to better cope with ‘fighting on the move’.
[*] Melee damage adjustments have been rebalanced across all weapons. The bonus from meleeing from behind has been reduced to 25% (down from 50%). The ‘value’ of melee damage adjustments from modules has been doubled (most modules that adjust melee damage have had their adjustments cut in half to compensate). Additionally, shields now take 20% less damage from melee.
[*] Damage from sticky bombs and HE grenades have been increased. This was actually due to a bug, so it’s more like, “they’ve been returned to their intended values”.
[*] The Surge Beam can now also repair shields at a 75% rate.
[/list]
[h3]Perks[/h3]
[list]
[*] A new perk has been added: Power Insurance. This is unlocked when you reach level 7. While having this perk equipped, you will only drop 50% of all carried power when you die.
[*] The Power Efficiency perk that used to be unlocked at level 7 can now instead be unlocked with Favour from a vendor.
[*] The Power Efficiency perk now also reduces the cost of using ‘boost stations’ (Health Regeneration, Shield Regeneration, and Shield Upgrades).
[*] The highlighting from the Acidic Tracker perk now only lasts 5 seconds (down from 10).
[/list]
[h3]Vehicles[/h3]
[list]
[*] The murder wagon panels are now more vulnerable to explosives.
[*] Driving through fire or spore clouds will no longer affect you with their DOTs. Note that being shot by an incendiary or spore projectile will still affect you as normal, even if in a vehicle.
[*] Vehicle ramming now deals 20% less damage to shields.
[/list]
[h3]Creatures[/h3]
[list]
[*] The burrower boss has received a number of updates: It’s been dressed up a bit. Its target selection behaviour has been improved. It now summons a lot more juveniles when reaching half health. Its different hit zones have been assigned more appropriate damage modifiers and destructible parts have been set up.
[*] Hitzones around the head and frill of the gorlizard have been improved to have more accurate hit registrations.
[*] The red defender drone has been made a bit tougher.
[/list]
[h2]Game Mode[/h2]
[list]
[*] The winning/best team is now declared at the end of a match.
[*] Survival related bonus rewards have been removed.
[*] What used to be distributed to survivors is now completely given to the ‘winning’ team (i.e. whichever team had the most resources extracted, with score as a tiebreaker).
[*] To go with the ‘winning team’ update, the score for taking down bosses has been increased and the score for opening a keycard door has been reduced.
[*] If your team is carrying a resource when the match times out, you now get 250 bonus score.
[*] Resource points now take 2 minutes to capture, down from 3.
[*] The shields awarded from resource points have changed; see the points below for more details.
[*] Gorlizard resource points always give out tier 3 shields (down from tier 4).
[*] The machine resource points give out shields based on which objective they are: Objective A gives a tier 2 (down from tier 4); Objective B gives a tier 3 (down from tier 4); Objective C (and beyond, when applicable) gives a tier 4 (same as before).
[*] The surface will now have three supply stations instead of two. They will always be spaced apart to reduce the variance in distance from starting points.
[*] Supply stations no longer sell tier 1 shields; they will at least be tier 2.
[*] If you die without unlocking a shield, you will now always be respawning with a tier 1 shield.
[*] NPCs now drop a lot more shields; higher tier shields from stronger creatures.
[*] When gorlizards drop shields, they now always drop two of them.
[*] The lost supply crates in the forest no longer give shields, but instead a guaranteed weapon.
[*] The prevalence of tier 4 shields has been slightly reduced: They drop less frequently from red cattermaws; they are less likely to appear in drop boxes; the ‘Shield Upgrade’ event in the labs is less likely to be active.
[*] In order to reduce the frequency of overlapping AoE types in the same match, a match now randomly restricts one or two (equal chance) AoE weapon types from being able to appear in that match (as random loot or from supply stations). When a type is restricted, all variants of that type will be removed from the match. These types are: All toxic plasma rifles; all cluster strike snipers; all energy bombers. Custom weapons are unaffected.
[*] Vehicles will now automatically spawn inside your forward camps. As soon as one is driven out, a new one spawns in its place. You can only claim a vehicle from your own team’s forward camp.
[*] The team upgrade that lets you summon a 3-seater from a forward camp now has a 5-minute cooldown.
[*] The in-game match objective will now automatically update to the most relevant resource. For example, if your team picks up ‘B’ when ‘A’ is still in play, ‘B’ will become your main objective.
[*] The weapon replicator event now creates weapons at 3 power per second (up from 2).
[*] Kills are now awarded to the player who downed a target, even if another teammate finishes the kill. If a player of a different team finishes the victim, they get the kill.
[/list]
[h2]Onboarding[/h2]
[list]
[*] The previous tutorial has been deleted and replaced with a new one.
[*] Starter weapons on the loadout screen should now come with descriptions to better explain how they play.
[*] The ‘Wild Hunt’ onboarding mission now only requires you to kill 5 creatures in the wilderness, down from 10.
[*] You can no longer matchmake for a game if you have a pending onboarding mission that is waiting in the lobby, but will instead be told what you need to do.
[*] The onboarding infographic missions have been completely reworked. Most of them now show short videos instead of still images. Their text has been refined to be shorter. Players who want to know more have a ‘More Info’ option that allows them to dig deeper.
[*] The loading screen now shows tips and hints.
[*] Messaging when interacting with vendors during onboarding has been made clearer.
[/list]
[h2]General Gameplay[/h2]
[list]
[*] The Cattermaw (the snail-like creature) has been given a new model, animations, sounds, etc. including a few behaviour changes.
[*] Many more achievements have been added.
[*] Various performance optimisations.
[*] You will now automatically stop matchmaking if you leave a party.
[*] Removed one of the voice options that was too close to the “announcer” voice, in order to make objective call-outs easier to make out.
[*] The climbing system has been completely reworked. It should resolve various interaction issues and also be more consistent. Additionally, you should now be able to climb into crawl spaces (e.g. through windows or into vents), as opposed to climbing past them.
[*] Automatic “creature clean-up” in the forest has been reworked. They should no longer despawn if there are players nearby, even if the creature in question can’t be seen by anyone.
[*] Pinging the enemy markers on surveillance maps (i.e. the air strike, EMP, blast door, or toxic release maps) will now properly apply an in-world ping marker at that player’s last known location. This was actually a bug, but it didn’t work at all, so might as well be highlighted as a “new feature”.
[*] Vehicle ‘ownership’ has been reworked. If a player goes from one vehicle to another, those vehicles will swap owner instead of simply deleting the old one.
[*] The “one-seater quad bikes” can now seat three players (i.e. the small vehicles you can pick up from your forward camp). Up to two other players can now cling on to the sides as you drive.
[*] Vehicle look now inherits your aim sensitivity settings.
[*] You will now automatically stop crouching if you try to sprint (and there is enough space to stand).
[*] Sliding now loses velocity less quickly (i.e. you maintain speed for longer) and you can freely look around while sliding (previously, a slide would be interrupted if you turned backwards). There are still a few kinks with this we want to work through to make it feel better, so it’s still a bit of a “work in progress”.
[*] If you stand back up during a slide, you will carry on sprinting (assuming you were sprinting when you first started the slide).
[*] The sliding sound has had its volume reduced.
[*] The breathing animation from the first person unarmed view has been removed to avoid motion sickness.
[*] The hitbox sizes for most pick-ups have been increased to make them easier to pick up while on the move.
[/list]
[h2]Level Updates[/h2]
[list]
[*] A large amount of cliffs and rocks around the entire forest have been reworked to better interact with the new climbing system.
[*] A lot of old doors have been updated to be more consistent in size and placement.
[*] Key-card doors have been given a unique appearance. In some cases, this has resulted in complete redesigns of the key-card rooms to better make use of the space.
[*] The large apartment and maintenance tunnels under the plantation have been completely removed and replaced with a new, more easily identifiable gameplay space. This new moulding facility is directly connected to the roadway tunnels running under the vaults. It can also contain a brand new resource capture point.
[*] The building above water treatment has been replaced with a completely new, more easily identifiable building: a two-story creature lab. The Gorlizard resource point will now spawn inside this building instead of the container outside.
[*] The comms tower on the north east side of the shade has been replaced by a brand new building with a more distinguishable resource point area and more easily accessible supply station.
[*] The area between the central control tower and thermal transfer has been made more easily traversable. More climbing spots have been added to scale the walls, along with a few ladders for the taller sections. The tree root up to the tower has been replaced with a ladder in partial cover.
[*] The upstairs layout of the cryo chamber area has been completely redesigned to be less confusing.
[*] Added more looting areas and cover items to the ‘land harbour’ area on the south side of the tree.
[*] The inside of the thermal transfer building has been slightly reworked to make it easier to navigate around.
[*] The pod buildings in the forest have been deleted and replaced with some new designs that should provide some better combat spaces and be easier to navigate.
[*] The large bridge across the ravine has been swapped out for a new bridge and the area it goes out to has been reworked to provide a new path through the mountain ridge and some high ground to vary up the combat spaces down the natural corridors.
[*] Forward camps have been slightly adjusted to make them easier to move around in.
[*] The airstrike battery building has been given some handy stairs to make it easier to get up to the catwalk.
[*] The vault hatch by the hangar gate has been reworked to be smoother to move around and over.
[*] A lot of updates to cover item placement across the shade (central surface area) and roadways underground.
[*] Various climbing points throughout the whole map have been improved.
[*] The crater base on the south side of the map has been reworked to be more on par with other potential starting points when it comes to high-ground defence and quicker repositioning.
[*] Thanks to some bug fixes, we could fine tune the exact locations of various ‘resource point contest’ thresholds. For example, you should no longer be able to contest the canteen bathroom resource point while half-way through a vent; you have to properly enter the room to contest it.
[*] More speakers have been added throughout the vault to make audio broadcasts easier to pick up on.
[*] A number of secrets have been scattered around the lobby.
[/list]
[h2]UI[/h2]
[list]
[*] There is now some rudimentary text chat in the game. For the time being, it’s very barebones but more functionality will be coming. In the lobby, default text chat is public. In a match, default text chat goes only to your team.
[*] While using beam gloves, you can now see your allies’ shield bars (in addition to the health bar) above their heads.
[*] The UI for supply stations has been completely redone. They’ve been given a cleaner, more easy-to-read look in general. Items should be easier to identify from a distance. Buttons should be easier to interact with from weird angles. Item unlock buttons should now make it clearer if you have already unlocked an item or, in case of shields, if you have already unlocked a stronger shield.
[*] Player names in the lobby will now fade out as they get further away.
[*] Power and Life icons in the UI have been made clearer.
[*] The ‘Respawn’ button should now be clearer and also warn you when you respawn on your last life.
[*] Lobby weapons can now be equipped directly from the crafting screen.
[*] The systems running the UI have been entirely reworked; partially to make our own lives easier but should also result in some performance improvements as well as edge case bug fixes. Here’s hoping we’ve caught all the issues!
[*] ‘Level Up’, ‘New Mission’, and ‘Mission Complete’ fanfares have been redesigned to be more noticeable.
[*] New pop-ups for ‘new unlocks’ have been created.
[*] The ‘Team Stats’ tab has been removed from the end-of-match screen. The score breakdown has been integrated into the reward screen instead. The player stats can still be seen on the ‘All Team Stats’ screen.
[*] The ‘Close’, ‘Medium’, and ‘Far’ ADS sensitivity settings now instead show which zoom levels they apply to.
[*] The logo and loading spinners have been given an overhaul.
[*] Changing forward camp will now automatically update your respawn point to the new forward camp if your previous respawn point was the now-previous forward camp. Does that sentence make sense…?
[/list]
[h2]Bug Fixes[/h2]
[list]
[*] You should no longer be able to send a 3-floor lift to a floor that happens to be sealed off in a match.
[*] Players will no longer make ‘pain’ sounds if shot by an ally.
[*] The shield panel in the forward camp should be properly attached to the wall again.
[*] The burrower boss should no longer fully burrow in the middle of combat unless it can’t get to its targets.
[*] The hole in the map in the corner of the thermal transfer building when the reactor is sealed should now be properly blocked up.
[*] Fixed various spots in the underground where you were able to look down narrow angles and see past unloaded sublevels.
[*] When unlocking shotguns, you will now be provided with matching magazine and ammo modules.
[*] The gorlizard that can spawn in the hangar containment should no longer be active before the door has been opened.
[*] Corrected a few weapon module power costs.
[*] Stopped wildlife from spawning inside of rocks or walls. Except one particular rock that seems to attract drones, for some as of yet unknown reason.
[*] Fixed some nav mesh issues for NPCs.
[*] Fixed a race condition that could happen with weapon swapping and shooting on high ping.
[*] Melee around walls and tight spaces (e.g. in vents) should be more consistent.
[*] The Brawler perk should no longer multiplicatively stack with the damage bonus from melee attacks from behind.
[*] Multiple nearby sources of firing audio should no longer cancel each other out.
[*] Fixed an issue with player name plates getting duplicated.
[*] EMP effects now linger on shields even if you drop and pick them back up.
[*] Defender drones should now be able to damage you even if you crouch underneath them.
[*] Beam glove damage on cattermaw that retreat into their shells should now behave properly.
[*] Beam targeting should now be more consistent against gorlizards.
[*] Changing the resolution slider should no longer break sniper scopes.
[*] The respawn map will no longer automatically change floors as teammates move through other respawn points on other floors.
[*] Team upgrades will now play the correct audio when unlocked.
[*] The vehicle camera should no longer be able to escape through the ceiling of the underground vaults.
[*] Fixed an issue with an indefinite loading screen if you try to reconnect to a match where you’ve lost all lives.
[*] Fixed some IK issues on the gorlizard.
[*] Fixed the alignment of a few blast doors.
[*] A mission completion fix for Vendor006.
[*] Fixed some dodgy alignment between the small waterfall towards the broken dam and the ground underneath.
[*] The minimap should now function when spectating a teammate.
[*] Fixed some camera jitters when manning a vehicle turret.
[*] Made exiting a vehicle a bit more reliable in regards to where you appear when there are blocking objects around you.
[*] In-world health bars that appear when you’re using beam gloves should now maintain a consistent width.
[*] Fixed a few pick-ups that overlapped with terrain or other blocking objects.
[*] The grenade-to-grenade collision volumes have been fixed.
[*] You should no longer be able to go immune to certain weapon types after swapping seats with enemies in vehicles.
[*] Certain doors behaved strangely if you alternated damaging and partially paying for them to open.
[*] The party UI should no longer fall out of sync if one party member disconnects during a match before returning to the lobby.
[*] Fixed a crash that could occur if you queued solo and then joined a party and queued up with them.
[*] Ability audio should now fall off properly over range.
[*] Items should no longer be able to fall into destructible boxes.
[/list]
